benchmarks.task_description:
fix(blofin): throw ArgumentsRequired from watchTickers without symbols

## Summary
`watchTickers()` without symbols threw `NotSupported`. The unified ws test runs the no-symbols and the one-symbol call together and only tolerates `ArgumentsRequired` for the first, so `NotSupported` ended the whole test and the call with symbols was never checked. Now it throws `ArgumentsRequired`, as kucoin/bithumb do and as `watchBidsAsks` in the same file already does via `marketSymbols`.

## Validation
- live `--ws watchTickers` JS + Py: the symbols call now runs and passes
- static ws 5 (JS + Py)

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(persons): show property edits on the person page after a reload

## Problem

- People who edit a person property see the old value on reload, although the edit saved. Reported in a [support ticket](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/01a1c77d-3152-0000-6a1c-d9588e279b62).

## Changes

- Reloading the person page now shows edits made seconds earlier.
- The person page loader now requests `force_blocking` instead of `blocking`.
- `blocking` served a pre-edit cached result for up to five minutes.
- No visual change, so no screenshot.

> [!NOTE]
> Each person page load now skips the cache and queries ClickHouse.

## How did you test this code?

- Manual check, not run: add a property on `/persons/<uuid>` and reload. It should show.
- CI complexity warning: on the unchanged `/person/*` URL handler.
- CI bundle size warning: the longer `refresh` value.

**Test rationale:** A new `personsLogic` test checks that loading by UUID requests `force_blocking`. No test covered a successful load before.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

**Skills:** `/adopting-generated-api-types`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/exploring-llm-traces`, `/review-code`

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** Claude Code with the PostHog MCP (query telemetry, read-only impersonation), the GitHub CLI and the Slack MCP.
- **Evidence:** Query telemetry for the reported case showed both reloads as cache hits on a result computed before the edit.
- **Decisions:** Ruled out ingestion lag, a stale ClickHouse person row and capture failures: the `$set` events reached the right person within seconds.
- **Decisions:** The persons list in `PersonsScene` keeps `blocking`, because its query is heavier and caching it still makes sense.
- **Decisions:** No open PR covers this. #99614, closed, surfaced capture errors, which is a different cause.
- **Public artifact:** The work started from a support ticket. The diff and this description carry no customer data.
- **Decisions:** Added the request-level test after the triage bot asked for one.
- **Decisions:** `personLogic` sends the same query and keeps `blocking`, after a PostHog Review finding. Its query path serves read-only popovers and notebook person nodes, which store only the person UUID. The query scans the team's `person_distinct_id2` rows. `refresh` is not part of the cache key, so a person page load also refreshes the entry those views read.
- **Read closely:** the `refresh` value in `loadPersonUUID`.

</details>

Read the engine corpus source as UTF-8 on every platform

The v0.1.13 release run (43210576472) failed on windows-x86_64 in `scripts/check-engine-behind.py`: `git show` output was decoded with the cp1252 default and hit a multi-byte character in carve-rs `tests/corpus.rs` (`UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x81`). No tag was created.

The subprocess call now decodes as UTF-8. The release-path tooling only; no shipped behavior changes, so no CHANGELOG entry.

+    def _get_wsman_connection_args(
+        self, ip_address, power_user, power_pass, port
+    ) -> tuple:
+        # Credentials are passed as separate options rather than embedded in
+        # an --endpoint URI because openwsman's URI parser can't handle
+        # special characters such as '@' in the password (LP: #2173566).
+        args = (
+            "--hostname",
+            ip_address,
+            "--port",
+            str(port),
+            "--username",
+            power_user,
+            "--password",
+            power_pass,
+            "--noverifypeer",
+            "--noverifyhost",
+            "--non-interactive",
+        )
+        if str(port) == AMT_HTTPS_PORT:
+            # DO NOT use --endpoint with HTTPS scheme because wsman's URI parser can't handle special characters such as '@' in the password (LP: #2173566).
+            # Instead, pass the CA cert via --cacert. This will trick wsman into using HTTPS, even though the endpoint URI is HTTP. This is a workaround for LP: #2173566.
+            # Note that we pass --noverify peer and --noverifyhost to avoid certificate verification issues, so the CA cert is not actually used for verification. It is only used to force wsman to use HTTPS.
+            args += ("--cacert", AMT_HTTPS_CACERT)
+        return args
+
